newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher amid commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher amid commercial buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher, and traders attributed nearby strength to commercial buying throughout the session.

Wheat gained early on lingering bullishness over the USDA's seedings report and on spillover support from CBOT soybeans. Gains were extended when Cargill Investors Services began buying March wheat during the session's second half.

"Shay was an early buyer of over a million March and it's speculated that it was commercial-related. Then CIS came in and began buying at $4.15 (per bushel). That firmed us up for the rest of the session," a KCBT trader said.
Cold weather in the Plains was not as much of a supporting factor as it was last week, and traders said the market seemed to be discounting recent fears of winterkill.

"The weekend is behind us, the temperatures this week are supposed to warm up and we may get additional snow," a trader said at the midsession. "I think that's why the market is 'cooling off' from last week's big talk (about winterkill)."
KCBT wheat settled 3-1/4 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 6-1/2 cents at $4.18 a bushel. New crop July gained five cents to close at $3.67.

Traders said CIS bought a total of 1.7 million July bushels while General Mills bought 1.5 million July and E D & F Man International bought 1.3 million May. Also, Shay Grain bought 1.5 million March and FIMAT sold 1.8 million March, sources said.
